correctness.rationale: Cartesian graph distance from the origin is D=sum_l l j_l. A radius-t unrolled neighbourhood without the individual root has identical initial color data in the regular vertex-transitive graph, so all D>t share one color. Every nonzero-distance coordinate on an odd cycle has exactly one predecessor closer to root; thus from a vertex of profile j, M=d-j0 predecessors carry profiles j-e_l+e_(l-1) with multiplicity j_l. The counts S_0=M j0+j1 and S_l=(M-1)j_l+j_(l+1) recursively recover j, ensuring layer-D profiles split at round D. This inductively proves the full intermediate partition. At round rd-1 all but the unique distance rd profile are already distinct; this last background is itself one profile and stable by automorphism orbit invariance. At rd-2 the rd-1 and rd profiles remain merged, proving sharpness. Sign reflections and coordinate permutations give transitive root stabilizer action on each profile; counting yields class sizes. Independent full-graph refinement on C5, C7, C9 powers (220 total test vertices) confirmed every intermediate partition and sizes.
residual_risks: Odd cycles length >=5 are essential to unique downward-neighbour property; even cycles fail this at antipodes.
Finite full-graph tests are corroboration; induction proves arbitrary r and d.
